songs.title: warm feels good again
songs.description: Warm soul pop for a cafe, A flat major, 96 BPM. Female low alto, half voice, near speech, as if humming to herself. Narrow melody in a fourth, one phrase returning; the chorus keeps those notes and lifts because the band opens, not because she pushes; lines end early. Rounded consonants, almost no vibrato. Full band, dense and soft: warm Wurlitzer, four-note motif, struck short; tape piano in short off-beat chords; one harmony voice, last chorus, no choir; round bass in short syncopated notes; soft kick, rim click, shaker every bar, never dropping out. Harmony Abmaj9 - Bbm9 - Cm9 - Dbmaj9 - Eb9 to Abmaj9, each chord a step above the last. Vocals behind the band, blended in, not upfront. Warm tone, softened top, tape warmth, lo-fi. Ends on a plucked chord, about two and a half minutes, the lyric filling all of it. One note per syllable, the band carrying every lift. No melisma, no sustained high notes, no head voice, no saxophone, no smoky bar or lounge, no autotune, no pop gloss.

songs.title: 흰 선
songs.description: Early-2000s Korean bright string-led pop, sung in Korean by a female mezzo, D4 to F4, warm and glowing, no male vocals, never belted, never strained, no rasp. F major, 110 BPM, light and rolling. Small strings lead with the hook in short bright bows, a steel-string acoustic guitar strumming beneath, a piano placing single notes between lines. Light kit: brushed backbeat, shaker, tambourine in the chorus. Strings from the first bar, the widest of the set. The final chorus opens into a wider brighter voicing, the one bright event, one decibel at most, no crescendo. Sweet walking delivery, slightly behind the beat, small vibrato at line ends only. Ending on a held chord, not a fade. The backing track has a dark top end with no cymbal sizzle. The voice keeps its natural breath and air, close-miked and present. Lead vocal clearly in front of the band. No English lyrics, no autotune, no trot, no K-pop gloss, no dance-pop synths. Bright airy modern mix, not retro.

Light kit: closed hi-hat in eighths, shaker, handclaps on two and four. A short rising bass run lands every chorus on a bright major ninth, the one bright event. No strings, a short bright plate. Busy conversational singing, pickups before the downbeat, slightly behind the beat, small vibrato at line ends only, no crescendo. He sings through to the final line, never drifting back. The backing track has a dark top end with no cymbal sizzle. The voice keeps its natural breath and air, close-miked and present. Lead vocal clearly in front of the band. No English lyrics, no autotune, no trot, no K-pop gloss, no sixteenth-note hi-hat. Bright airy modern mix, not retro.
